issues.where: the plinth and tabletop at 23.10–23.53 s
issues.what: The amber wash still shows the plinth silhouette, and the next clear view has a shell base and no pink tabletop scatter. The exterior handoff reads as a flash cut even though the clear frames do not show mixed seasons.
issues.fix: Keep the base, its reflection and the near-table scatter under the same moving veil as the glass. Change them at peak coverage and let the veil clear with the liquid.

issues.where: the suspended shake strokes at 22.23–23.10 s
issues.what: The collar rocks, but the globe stays at nearly the same lift height across the sampled strokes. Inside, the petals become a nearly uniform pink streak field, so the reversals lose both the weight of the globe and the lag of the liquid.
issues.fix: Give the sharper reversals unequal vertical dips and a delayed counter-tilt. Let the liquid visibly pile against the trailing wall and fold back before it fills the whole glass.

issues.where: the tabletop to the right of the shell base at 24.07–24.37 s
issues.what: After the base is down, the bright ground accent extends outward as a narrow strip with a moving leading edge. It reads more like a wipe than a response to the landing.
issues.fix: Start the ground response at contact, then build the reflected light and scattered grains together in patches that thin away from the base.

issues.where: the late gold motes around the tree and glass floor at 29.23–33.57 s
issues.what: The large whirl dies down, but the remaining particles are easier to read as hovering points of light than as grains finally coming to rest on the miniature.
issues.fix: Keep the ambient glow, but give a few foreground and background grains distinct slow falls and visible catches on the canopy, roof or floor.
